text:
Three of the messages Ines sends you across the next twelve hours are practical. The documentation package, how to carry it. The external review board, its timeline. The charter amendment process, the three clauses most worth pursuing.

The fourth message is longer.

It is not organised the way Ines's messages are usually organised. It does not have a subject line. It does not have bullet points. It reads like a letter that was written and not sent several times before this version, which you suspect is accurate.

She tells you about the first time she read the Commission summary. The year she spent believing the Archivist was the only person inside who understood what was being built. The message she sent through a third-party channel on a Tuesday night to a student she had never met because she had run out of other options. What she has been afraid of. What she has been hoping for, which is a different thing from the same list.

The last paragraph is: *Tomás should know all of it now. Not as a protection — we're past the point where knowing can protect him. As a right. He has been in this story the whole time. He should know what story he's been in.*

You read the message twice.

You put your phone in your pocket. You go to find him.
